rationale: Met describes repoussé marks worked into the back of a metal sheet with a tool to create a raised image on the front. This directly supports the prompt and explanation; distinct from chasing, engraving, and filigree.

Met explains that a raised design is finished by detailing the motif from the outside with a chisel, called chasing. This distinguishes front-side contour/detail work from 065’s back-side repoussé and from cutting/engraving.

Met supports metal lines cut directly with a burin into a plate to hold ink; it defines the burin’s beveled diamond tip cutting a groove and displacing a curl of metal. But the prompt only says ‘острый резец’ cutting recessed lines, which does not name or otherwise distinguish that burin mechanism from baseline 096 drypoint’s scratched line and burr. Specify штихель/бевелированный бурин and/or groove/curl mechanics to make the answer unique.
sourceLocator: Engraving definition and burin, lines 25–45; compare baseline `crafts-drypoint-burr` question

rationale: Getty AAT defines filigree as metalwork or metal decoration done entirely in fine wire, typically ornamenting precious metals or creating openwork. This matches the question and distinguishes it from raising, chasing, and engraving the sheet surface.

University of Iowa Printing Services says saddle-stitch/booklet-staple publications are stapled along the centerfold. That clearly distinguishes the method from sewing signatures, adhesive binding, and hard covers.

Princeton University Library describes Coptic binding as unsupported chain stitching linking each sewn section to the previous section across the spine, without sewing to cords. This distinctly separates it from centerfold staples and adhesive/hard binding.
sourceLocator: The Early Codex and Coptic Sewing, line 12

rationale: CraftHub/Design School Kolding says leno weave has two warp yarns woven around the weft, interlocking threads and creating open airy fabric. This distinguishes leno from double cloth, weft-loop pile, and raised extra-weft brocade.
